title: The Long Regiment
premise: Oscar Montrose, raised in the pearl-diving quarter and indentured to the Verrone Trading Company, has spent a lifetime making themselves useful and unremarkable. When a sealed letter from a dying clerk names Oscar's family as holders of a deed that could decide ownership of the harbor — and expose the company's wartime profiteering — Oscar becomes both evidence and target. As armistice negotiations stall, Oscar races to assemble testimony, ledgers, and witnesses into an official record before the victors' historians can bury or twist it. The book ends with the record accepted, the indentures voided, and Oscar choosing to stay with the improvised family of dockworkers, divers, and clerks who claimed them long before any inheritance did.
about_author: Silas Almeida is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port records and indenture ledgers along the old trade coasts. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia of those documents — the unsigned letters, the corrected entries, the names struck through but never quite erased.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Oscar Montrose, POV. A day in the counting-house: Oscar mends ledgers, fetches ink, and stays invisible while company men argue over war contracts. Flashbacks to their pearl-diver mother's drowning establish the debt that bound them to Verrone. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a hunger to belong somewhere by choice.

chapters.title: Ledger Margins
chapters.summary: Oscar notices numbers that don't reconcile — shipments logged as lost that clearly arrived. Old clerk Bramwell warns them to copy, not question. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: first crack in the company's authority; curiosity as dangerous inheritance.

chapters.title: The Dying Clerk
chapters.summary: Bramwell, feverish, presses a sealed letter into Oscar's hands: it names the Montrose family as lawful holders of the Harbor Deed, hidden during the war. He dies before explaining how. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: grief fused with dread — a gift that feels like a sentence.

chapters.title: What the Company Keeps
chapters.summary: Company factor Aldous Renner, POV. Renner learns Bramwell died and that something left his office unlogged. He orders a discreet search of the clerks' quarters. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace; the hunt begins without a name yet.

chapters.title: Salt and Kin
chapters.summary: Oscar hides the letter among their late mother's diving effects at the harbor tenement, where the diving community — Auntie Sefa, the Okafor brothers, young Teo — quietly absorbs them as one of their own. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: found family offered freely, contrasted with the indenture that owns them.

chapters.title: A Search Conducted Politely
chapters.summary: Renner's men ransack the clerks' wing; Oscar watches their mother's sea-chest nearly opened. They realize the letter must move again — or be read. First alliance: junior clerk Ivet, who owes Bramwell her position. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Deed Explained
chapters.summary: Ivet deciphers the letter: the Harbor Deed predates the company charter; whoever holds it can prove Verrone seized the docks under false wartime requisition — and profited from both sides. POV Ivet. Emotional beat: the scale of the truth, and why no faction wants it on record.

chapters.title: Every Side Wants Silence
chapters.summary: An emissary of the incoming victors' commission offers Oscar protection — for the deed, not for them. Simultaneously Renner offers freedom papers for silence. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: the seduction of easy exits; belonging tested against survival.

chapters.title: Teo Dives
chapters.summary: To prove the 'lost' cargo arrived, someone must recover the sunken requisition manifests from the scuttled barge Meridian. Teo, fourteen, insists he can dive the wreck. The tenement argues, then equips him. POV Teo. Emotional beat: the family risking itself for Oscar's cause — reciprocity of care.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Holds
chapters.summary: Teo's dive succeeds barely; the manifest tin is recovered but Renner's watchmen spot the boat. One Okafor brother is taken for questioning. POV Teo. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into guilt and urgency.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Renner questions the prisoner gently, which is worse than cruelty. He now suspects the Montrose name. POV Renner. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized — a man who believes order requires the lie.

chapters.title: The Armistice Clock
chapters.summary: News arrives: armistice talks resume in six weeks; afterward, a victors' historical commission will fix the official record permanently. Whatever isn't documented by then is dust. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: the deadline made flesh; the theme stated — history belongs to whoever writes it first.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ivet begin gathering testimony: a retired pilot, a customs widow, a Verrone boatswain with a conscience. Each witness costs something. POV Ivet. Emotional beat: the slow, unglamorous labor of truth-building; solidarity across class lines.

chapters.title: Renner's Counter-Record
chapters.summary: Renner begins drafting his own immaculate history, buying witnesses and backdating entries. He offers Ivet a promotion to betray the effort. She accepts — outwardly. POV Renner. Emotional beat: the archive as battlefield; double agent tension.

chapters.title: Betrayal or Bait
chapters.summary: Acting on Ivet's 'intelligence,' Renner raids a safehouse — and finds it empty, his own forged ledger pages photographed instead. But the raid burns a witness, who recants. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by real cost; trust strained.

chapters.title: The Mother's Proof
chapters.summary: Among the diving effects, Oscar finally reads their mother's letters properly: she witnessed the false requisition as a child, and Bramwell was her friend. The personal and legal inheritances are one. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into standing — Oscar stops being a messenger and becomes a claimant.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Auntie Sefa reveals she has known about the deed for decades and stayed silent to protect the divers from reprisal. Her anger at Oscar's risk-taking fractures the tenement. POV Sefa. Emotional beat: found family conflict — protection versus dignity.

chapters.title: Reconciliation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Teo mediates; Sefa concedes that silence bought safety but never belonging. The tenement commits fully: they will stand as witnesses publicly. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: the family chooses exposure together; belonging confirmed under threat.

chapters.title: The Commission Opens
chapters.summary: Armistice signed; the victors' historical commission convenes. Renner submits his polished record. Oscar requests standing to present a counter-record — and is nearly dismissed until the Harbor Deed's seal is verified. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: climax begins; the invisible made visible before power.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Climax: witness by witness — Ivet's documents, Teo's manifest, Sefa's testimony, the boatswain's confession — the counter-record dismantles Renner's version. Renner, confronted with his own backdated entries, does not deny them; he simply asks what good the truth ever did anyone. POV alternating Oscar/Renner. Emotional beat: truth prevailing not by force but by accumulation.

chapters.title: Papers
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the commission enters the counter-record; indentures tied to the fraudulent charter are voided. Oscar receives freedom papers — and finds them strangely light. Renner resigns rather than face prosecution, leaving one honest entry behind. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: victory's hollowness before its meaning settles.

chapters.title: The Long Regiment
chapters.summary: Resolution: Oscar declines a commission post, choosing instead to help found a people's archive above the tenement, staffed by divers, clerks, and children like Teo. The title's meaning lands: the long regiment is everyone who kept records alive when power wanted them blank. POV Oscar. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, inherited, and passed on.
